Testimony in Support of LD 945 ("An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Powers and Responsibilities of the Maine
Redevelopment Land Bank Authority")
J. Andrew Cashman on behalf of the Maine Association of REALTORS�
March 13, 2025
Senator Curry, Representative Gere and members of the Joint Select Committee on Housing and Economic Development, my name is Andy Cashman. I am the Founder of Resolve Government Relations. We represent the Maine Association of REALTORS�, a professional trade association established in 1936 with over 6,500 members statewide. REALTORS� grow Maine's economy and build Maine communities. Our members represent buyers and sellers involved in both residential and commercial real estate transactions. Our membership also includes industry affiliates, such as lenders, closing agents, title agents, appraisers, building inspectors, surveyors, etc. The Maine Association is chartered by the National Association of REALTORS� (NAR), the largest trade association in the country.
The Maine Association of REALTORS� supports LD 945 because it would encourage development of more units to meet our state's housing demands. This bill provides greater flexibility and reduces barriers for the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority to develop difficult properties throughout our state. The Redevelopment Land Bank focuses on repurposing and improving blighted, abandoned and environmentally hazardous properties to promote economic growth. Streamlining the ability for the Redevelopment Land Bank Authority to more efficiently develop property that would otherwise remain vacant or underdeveloped benefits the community through revitalization, improved property values and eventually more housing units for Mainers to call home.
We support this bill because it focuses on increasing opportunities for more housing in Maine. We do not have enough homes in Maine and need to develop more through low cost, low burden approaches such as LD 945. It would reduce some of the regulatory barriers that slow the conversion of Redevelopment Land Bank Authority properties. Development and revitalization contribute to a sound economic base. This is a common-sense approach to the overall improvement of communities which, in turn will attract new businesses, help to increase property values, and in turn, boosts local tax revenues. MAR supports measures that respond to the individual and collective housing needs of our society.
For these reasons, we respectfully urge the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on LD 945. Thank you for your time and consideration.

NEITHER FOR NOR AGAINST LD 945
An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Powers and Responsibilities of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority
March 13, 2025

Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development, my name is Judy East. I am the Director of the Bureau of Resource Information and Land Use Planning (BRILUP) within the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF). I am speaking neither for nor against LD 945, "An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Powers and Responsibilities of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority."
This bill amends various provisions of the laws governing the powers of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority. The Department appreciates the bill's intent to expand opportunities in which abandoned, blighted, functionally obsolete, environmentally hazardous, and other properties may be acquired for redevelopment.
DACF offers the following suggestions relative to the proposed requirement to have municipal and Land Use Planning Commission (LUPC) consent on the acquisition of property.
DACF notes that LUPC has neither legislative authority nor the administrative skill set to approve or disapprove land acquisition transactions. A comparable entity within the unorganized territories to the proposal for municipal consent of land acquisition transactions would be the county government. However, DACF notes that in land acquisitions for conservation by public entities or conservation organizations, neither municipalities nor counties are required to consent. We, therefore, question whether it is necessary or appropriate to require such consent for the acquisition of land for redevelopment purposes.
Thank you for your time. I would be happy to answer any questions now or at the work session.

Testimony of Representative Melanie Sachs introducing
LD 945, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Powers and Responsibilities of the Maine
Redevelopment Land Bank Authority Before the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development
Senator CUITY, Representative Gere and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Housing and Economic Development, my name is Melanie Sachs and I am honored to represent
the community of Freepoit in the Maine Legislature.
I am before you today to introduce LD 945, An Act to Amend the Laws Governing the Powers
and Responsibilities of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority, a bill submitted on behalf of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority (MRLBA).
I sponsored the original legislation in the 130"` to establish the MRLBA. It passed due to the
incredibly hard work of many bipartisan members of this committee and the Legislature, along with a broad and diverse coalition of partners across the state. I know the Executive Director, Tuck O'Brien, has briefed this committee on the extraordinary scope of issues and guidance it has provided to Maine communities all across the state in just a short period of time. Its potential is enonn0us- just what we envisioned when the legislation was passed. It is prudent for the Redevelopment Authority's Board and staff, now that it has been operating for a period, to
suggest thoughtful, clarifying adjustments to its statute, and to bring those to this committee for
review. The specific changes will be discussed in depth by the Executive Director in his
testimony.
Thank you for your time and for the opportunity to submit this bill for your consideration.

Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development:
My name is Bob Bryant and I'm pleased to testify today in support of LD 945, An Act to Amend the Laws

Governing the Powers and Responsibilities of the Maine Redevelopment Land BankAuthority.
I was born and raised in Pittsfield, ME and graduated from Maine Central Institute in 1978. After college at St. Mike's in VT, a stint in the US Navy, and with an MBA from Bryant University, I was fortunate enough to have a long career in Information Technology that took me to many places across the US and the world. However, I always came home to Maine. Over my career when I came back to the place that created my basis in life, I watched as vibrant and thriving communities I knevv as a child fell into
economic turmoilwhen companies that once supported Central and Northern Maine pulled their operations, while leaving behind manufacturing buildings they no longer wanted and the people they no
longer needed. When I retired from IT, I moved back home with a goal of trying to help those
i
communities.
I now live in Hartland, ME, one of those very communities whose manufacturing history and economic health was lost when Irving Tanning went bankrupt, the State took over the mortgage, and Tasman
Tanning decided it no longer wanted to operate in Hartland despite significant tax breaks and vastly under
market lease costs. Imagine my delight to hear of the establishment of the Land Bank by the Maine Legislature in 2022. I immediately submitted myself and my experience for consideration as the District
2 Commissioner. I was fortunate enough to gain both the Governor's Appointment and the Senate's
l
Confirmation.
Since that time, I've been engaged with nine dedicated, enthusiastic, and highly experienced
professionals, vvho along with our ex-officio members from various State of Maine agencies are focused on one thing: bringing abandoned and blighted buildings back to valued tax bearing properties for the
communities and people of Maine.
We I ve done a lot of work and have positively impacted several communities already, but'we're just getting started. And as is common in initial creations of organizations through legislative action, there are areas
in the original legislation that need clarification to ensure efficient and effective operation of the Land Bank.
First, the Land Bank needs explicit corporate powers so its operations and governance can be properly operated by the Commission.
Second, we need clarification that the Land Bank was created to take over both publicly and privately owned and even federal properties to ensure efficient transfer of real estate. Many municipalities don't have the resources or the capabilities to take over blighted properties. And these properties can come from many sources. The legislature created the Land Bank to help municipalities by direct interaction with problem properties to bring them back to productive and tax-paying entities. Frankly, the tannery in

Hartland is one such property, and without the Land Bank's help and resources to affect changes to it, it will only continue to be a blight on the town, forestalling economic progress.
These items, while implicit in the original legislation, need to be clarified, which is what LD 945 will do for
the Land Bank so we may expand the good work we're doing for the communities and people of Maine.
Thank you for your time today and your continued support for the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank
Authority.

Testimony of Tuck O'Brien, Executive Director, Maine Redevelopment Land Bank
Authority in support of LD 945 "An Act to Amend the Laws Governing th,e Powers and
Responsibilities of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority" before the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development.
March 13, 2025
Senator Curry, Representative Gere and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing
and Economic Development:
My name is Tuck O'Brien, and I have the incredible privilege to be the first Executive
Director of the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Authority. As Representative Sachs
mentioned, I come before you today to urge your support for the passage of LD 945, which
would adopt several clarifying revisions to the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Act.
Over the past eight months, we've traveled across Maine---from Madawaska to Kittery and Jonesport to Rumford--engaging with communities and listening to their challenges. From this, we've gained invaluable insights into the real~world implications of our statute. The proposed technical changes are straightforward and aim to enable the legislation to work
as intended by streamlining to minimize legal and financial risks to our municipal partners while allowing Maine Redevelopment to more efficiently meet their needs.
We crafted these changes with guidance of legal counsel, our municipal partners and many of the people involved with the creation of the statute, several of whom are in the
room today. These revisions include:
1. Adding General Corporate Powers - While this key operating element for quasi-
governmental entities is referenced in several places, it is currently missing from the body of the statute. The addition of general corporate powers codifies that Maine Redevelopment can perform actions such as acquiring and selling property, making loans, and forming partnerships. This change aligns our statutory purpose with our enumerated powers and mirrors language for similar authorities, like the
-
Loring Development Authority and Maine Connectivity Authority.

2. Clarifying Municipal Collaboration -This revision aims to make the statute more
explicit about the acquisition process, allowing Maine Redevelopment to obtain eligible properties that are not yet municipally owned by negotiating directly with
-
third parties. This approach minimizes legal and financial risks for municipalities
while enabling transactions to proceed smoothly. Additionally, we incorporate a
clear requirement for municipal consent, ensuring that local governments stay informed and maintain a degree of oversight in alignment with our mission.
3. Removing references to the Development Ready Advisory Committee -- This committee is being appropriately shifted to the Maine Office of Community Affairs
(MOCA).

Across our state, too many properties remain vacant, deteriorating, and unfit for

productive use. These sites aren't just eyesores; they drain municipal budgets, pose public

health and safety risks, and obstruct economic growth, particularly in communities that

need support the most. Maine Redevelopment was created to change that reality by

providing technical and financial support to help communities bring these properties back

to productive use.

.

By working directly with municipalities, we help overcome the various barriers to
redevelopment--whether they are legal, financial, or environmental. We're already seeing
momentum with ourfirst projects in East Millinocket and Van Buren, and are actively
evaluating projects in seven other communities. These projects arejust the beginning.
With continued support and collaboration, we can expand our impact statewide, turning
properties once viewed as burdens into engines of renewal and growth.

In conclusion, the proposed revisions to the Maine Redevelopment Land Bank Act will help

us operate more effectively, reduce risks, and enhance our ability to support

municipalities across the state. I urge you to support LD 945 and continue to empower

Maine communities in their efforts to revitalize abandoned properties and foster economic

growth.
